description: Des sujets à dire à voix haute, comme à l'examen : décrire, réagir à l'imprévu, donner son avis. On retourne la carte pour voir une réponse type.

fiches.question: Describe your aircraft to someone who has never flown.
fiches.reponse: Say what kind of aircraft it is, how many engines and seats, how far and how high it flies, and one thing you like about flying it.

fiches.question: Explain how you prepare a flight, from the briefing to engine start.
fiches.reponse: Weather, NOTAMs and flight plan; fuel decision; aircraft documents and technical log; crew briefing; walk-around; cockpit preparation; clearance; start-up.

fiches.question: Describe the weather on a day you remember well.
fiches.reponse: Give the season and the place, the cloud, wind and visibility, how it changed, and how it affected the flight.

fiches.question: Explain the difference between an altitude and a flight level.
fiches.reponse: An altitude is measured on QNH, above sea level; a flight level is measured on 1013.25 hPa, in hundreds of feet.

fiches.question: Describe what happens during a pushback.
fiches.reponse: The ground crew connects the tug, the crew gets clearance, releases the brakes on request, starts engines during or after the push, and sets the parking brake at the end.

fiches.question: Explain why de-icing matters before take-off.
fiches.reponse: Even thin frost spoils the airflow over the wing, raises the stall speed and can stop the aircraft from flying; the fluid only protects for its holdover time.

fiches.question: Describe your airport to a pilot who has never been there.
fiches.reponse: Runways and their length, terrain and obstacles, usual approaches, taxi hot spots, weather traps, and where the stands are.

fiches.question: Explain how TCAS works and what the crew does after an RA.
fiches.reponse: It interrogates other transponders, warns of traffic and gives a climb or descend order; the crew follows it at once, tells ATC « TCAS RA », and reports « clear of conflict » afterwards.

fiches.question: You hit a bird on climb out and one engine vibrates. Tell ATC what happened and what you want.
fiches.reponse: Pan pan, bird strike on climb out, vibration on the left engine, we would like to level off at 5000 feet, run our checklist and probably return; we will advise.

fiches.question: A passenger has collapsed and the doctor on board wants to land. Ask for a diversion.
fiches.reponse: We have a passenger with a suspected heart attack, a doctor on board asks to land as soon as possible, request diversion to the nearest suitable airport and an ambulance on arrival.

fiches.question: Your flaps are stuck at 5 degrees. Explain the consequences to ATC.
fiches.reponse: Our flaps are jammed, we need a faster approach speed and a longer runway, about 2500 metres, and some time in a hold to prepare.

fiches.question: There is smoke in the cabin. Give ATC the essentials in one message.
fiches.reponse: Mayday mayday mayday, smoke in the cabin, descending to 10000 feet, request immediate return and fire services on the runway, 154 souls on board, 2 hours of fuel.

fiches.question: The controller gives you a clearance you do not understand. Ask for clarification.
fiches.reponse: Sorry, I did not understand: do you want us to descend now or after the waypoint? Please say again slowly.

fiches.question: An unruly passenger is threatening the crew. Inform ATC.
fiches.reponse: We have a disruptive passenger who is threatening the crew, he is now restrained, we request police to meet the aircraft on arrival.

fiches.question: Your radio fails, then comes back. Explain to ATC what you did meanwhile.
fiches.reponse: We lost both radios for about ten minutes, we squawked 7600 and kept to our last clearance, the radios are back now.

fiches.question: A thunderstorm sits on your route. Ask for a deviation and explain.
fiches.reponse: We have a big cell on our weather radar ahead, request 20 miles right of track to avoid it, we will tell you when we can return.

fiches.question: You are low on fuel because of holding. Explain your fuel state.
fiches.reponse: We have held for 30 minutes, we can hold 15 more minutes, then we must divert; if we are delayed further we will declare minimum fuel.

fiches.question: After landing you think you overran a light on the runway. Report it.
fiches.reponse: We think we may have hit a runway light during the rollout, you may want to check the runway before the next landing.

fiches.question: What do you think of automation in the cockpit?
fiches.reponse: Give both sides: it reduces workload and errors, but pilots can lose manual skills and awareness; finish with what you do to stay sharp.

fiches.question: Should pilots retire at a fixed age? Give your opinion.
fiches.reponse: Say yes or no, give two reasons, mention medical checks, and suggest a compromise.

fiches.question: How has aviation changed since you started flying?
fiches.reponse: Talk about technology, traffic, rules and training, with one personal example.

fiches.question: What makes a good captain?
fiches.reponse: Leadership without pressure, clear communication, sharing tasks, listening to the crew, calm decisions.

fiches.question: Is flying good or bad for the environment? Discuss.
fiches.reponse: Recognise the emissions, mention newer engines, sustainable fuels and single-engine taxi, and give your own view.

fiches.question: Tell me about a difficult decision you made as a pilot.
fiches.reponse: Set the scene, explain the options, what you chose and why, and what you learned.

fiches.question: How do you deal with fatigue on long or night flights?
fiches.reponse: Rest before the duty, controlled rest when allowed, light meals and water, cross-checking, speaking up when tired.

fiches.question: What do you do to keep your English at level 6?
fiches.reponse: Listening to radio and podcasts, reading aviation news, speaking with colleagues, practising unusual situations.
